items.title: Australian facilities damaged in Iranian attack on Middle East air base
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that an Iranian projectile hit a road just outside the Al Minhad Air Base, but no Australians were injured.

items.title: Live: Iran vows 'decisive' revenge for killing of Larijani
items.description: Iran vows revenge for the killing of its top national security adviser, Ali Larijani. Meanwhile, Anthony Albanese says Australian facilities have been damaged in an Iranian attack on a Middle East air base. Follow live.

items.title: Resignations and refusals: Trump increasingly isolated in Iran war
items.description: After years of threats, insults and throwing the global world order into chaos, Donald Trump is being reminded at home and abroad that trust isn't just a nicety, it's essential when you need allies.

items.title: Australia's fuel shipments look safe for the next month. After that, it's complicated
items.description: Ships carrying oil are continuing to come to Australia as expected and should do so for the next month, and the industry is urging that while the picture beyond that is uncertain and complicated, "the tankers have never stopped coming".

items.title: High fuel costs from Iran war force Aussies to cancel road trips, cruises
items.description: Domestic travel is also taking a hit as a result of rising fuel costs across the globe, with regional communities likely to feel the most impact.

items.title: Sydney resident fears for cousin facing 'unjustified' charges in Iran
items.description: Iranian Australians with family in Iran are concerned for their loved ones, with internet and phone blackouts making it near-impossible to stay in contact.

items.title: Cyclone Narelle 'likely' to be category five before landfall in Qld, BOM says
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle could threaten Queensland coast as a severe category five system this week.

items.title: Body-in-suitcase double murderer appeals life sentences
items.description: Daniel Holdom is appealing his life sentences for dumping the body of a toddler in a suitcase after he killed her and her mother.

items.title: Sacked Sandilands says network decided to 'burn the place down'
items.description: Kyle Sandilands has announced he has been sacked by ARN Media after an on-air row with co-host Jackie Henderson last month.

items.title: Chronic conditions dismissed as anxiety, low iron
items.description: Young women have detailed their experiences being dismissed and misdiagnosed as chronic pain sufferers. Now, they're teaching others how to advocate for their health.

items.title: BHP and Woodside appoint new CEOs in major mining shake-up
items.description: BHP has tapped Brandon Craig as its new CEO, while Elizabeth Westcott has taken the top job at Woodside Energy three months after she served as acting CEO.

items.title: Liberals defend flyer that confused Palestinian flag with another
items.description: The South Australian Liberals have defended an election campaign flyer that attacks a Labor MP for his views on the Middle East and carries the slogan "Defend Australian Values", but appears to mistakenly show an image of a Sudanese flag instead of a Palestinian one.

items.title: Rescued kayaker 'didn't panic' despite going missing overnight
items.description: A lost kayaker who spent the night on a sandbank in waters north of Adelaide has driven himself home and says he is "happy to be alive and well", after being rescued on Wednesday.

items.title: US rapper's 'inflammatory' comments at Sydney festival condemned
items.description: In a video uploaded to social media, Zubeyda Muzeyyen, known as DJ Haram, can be heard urging attendees to "oppose the Zio-Australian-Epstein empire" before she led the crowd with a chant.

items.title: Which hand soap is best for killing germs?
items.description: Experts say there is an array of options when it comes to hand soaps, and some labels can be misleading.

items.title: 'You have to laugh': Why this critique of corporate work culture is a comedy
items.description: This dark comedy takes aim at capitalism and corporate work culture, but it also finds hope in the relationships between everyday people.

items.title: The traditional granny flat is changing, and Tasmania is leading the way
items.description: Tasmanians will soon be able to build second dwellings that are 50 per cent larger than the current size. An urban planner says other jurisdictions should follow suit.

items.title: To fix the generation gap, Labor may have to leave the grandfathers behind
items.description: A Senate committee report into the capital gains tax was authored by the Greens but littered with clues about Labor's plans.

items.title: RBA governor warns of the recession we might have to have
items.description: Is the RBA fighting last year's inflation war with its latest interest rate hike? Whatever the case may be, Australians are bracing for even more economic pain.

items.title: Live: Chance of RBA interest rate hike in May drops to 40pc, ASX rises
items.description: The Australian share market is trading slightly higher, while the likelihood of a follow-up interest rate hike in May has fallen substantially after the Reserve Bank's 5-4 vote in favour of yesterday's rate increase — the slimmest of majorities. Follow live.

items.title: Court transcription service in crisis after entering voluntary administration
items.description: Four weeks after the ABC revealed sensitive court files were being accessed offshore in a potential risk to national security, the company responsible for the breach has entered into voluntary administration.

items.title: Bank of America reaches tentative settlement over Epstein-related lawsuit
items.description: Bank of America has tentatively settled a lawsuit claiming it ignored suspicious financial transactions involving Jeffrey Epstein while he was sexually abusing hundreds of girls and women.

items.title: Federal government loses bid to monitor those released from immigration detention
items.description: New government measures to monitor people released from indefinite immigration detention are struck down by the High Court in Canberra.

items.title: Man shot at cafe, getaway car burnt in incident linked to illegal tobacco
items.description: Police are investigating whether a 49-year-old man shot in Altona North in Melbourne's west was a random victim of the illegal tobacco trade or was targeted by the offenders.

items.title: Organised crime link to Yarra Valley worker exploitation
items.description: The Labour Hire Authority has accused an apple grower and labour-hire business of exploiting workers in the Yarra Valley, as concerns emerge about organised crime links.
